'''Anita Goel''' is an American [[physicist]], [[physician]], and [[scientist]] in the emerging field of Nanobiophysics. At the Nanobiosym Research Institute (NBS), Goel examines the physics of life and the way nanomotors read and write information into DNA.

==Education==
Goel received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] and M.A. in physics from [[Harvard University]], where she worked with [[Nobel Prize|Nobel laureate]] [[Dudley R. Herschbach]]. Her thesis was entitled ''Single Molecule Dynamics of Motor Enzymes Along DNA''.

She received a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in physics with honors and distinction from [[Stanford University]], where her honors thesis mentor was Nobel laureate [[Steven Chu]].

She also earned in parallel an [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] from the Harvard–[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] Joint Division of Health Sciences and Technology (HST).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nanobiosym.com/our-team/chairman-and-ceo.html |title=About our chairman and CEO |access-date=2014-09-03 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140904031551/http://www.nanobiosym.com/our-team/chairman-and-ceo.html |archive-date=2014-09-04 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.technologyreview.com/tr35/?year=2005 |title=2005 Young Innovators Under 35 |publisher=[[Technology Review]] | year=2005 | access-date=August 15, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.geneticsandhealth.com/2005/12/09/dr-anita-goel-studying-dna-using-physics/|title=Genetics and Health » Dr. Anita Goel - Studying DNA Using Physics|date=26 March 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060326082457/http://www.geneticsandhealth.com/2005/12/09/dr-anita-goel-studying-dna-using-physics/ |access-date=21 July 2022|url-status=usurped|archive-date=2006-03-26 }}</ref>

==Career==
Goel has over 80 patents worldwide and has published in journals including ''Nature Nanotechnology''<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1038/nnano.2008.190 | title=Harnessing biological motors to engineer systems for nanoscale transport and assembly | year=2008 | last1=Goel | first1=Anita | last2=Vogel | first2=Viola | journal=Nature Nanotechnology | volume=3 | issue=8 | pages=465–475 | pmid=18685633 | bibcode=2008NatNa...3..465G | doi-access=free }}</ref> and ''Scientific American''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/anita-goel/|title=Stories by Anita Goel|website=Scientificamerican.com|access-date=21 July 2022}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and the "Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)."<ref>{{cite journal|title=Tuning DNA "strings": Modulating the rate of DNA replication with mechanical tension|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=2001 |doi=10.1073/pnas.151261198 |last1=Goel |first1=Anita |last2=Frank-Kamenetskii |first2=Maxim D. |last3=Ellenberger |first3=Tom |last4=Herschbach |first4=Dudley |volume=98 |issue=15 |pages=8485–8489 |doi-access=free |pmid=11447284 |pmc=37462 |bibcode=2001PNAS...98.8485G }}</ref>

She has testified in the US Senate for the $1.5 Billion dollar National Nanotechnology Initiative;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commerce.senate.gov/services/files/0C92EBBB-BA9A-4734-B34B-5EB8E6ABCD0B|title=Testimony of Anita Goel, MD, PhD|website=Commerce.senate.gov|access-date=21 July 2022}}</ref> advised President Obama's PCAST for his Strategy for American Innovation; served on the Triennial Review Board of the National Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/microsites/ostp/PCAST/2016_nrc_review_of_the_nni_part_1.pdf|title=2016 Triennial Review of the National Nanotechnology Initiative|website=Obamawhitehouse.archives.gov|access-date=21 July 2022}}</ref>

She was invited by the late MIT President Chuck Vest to serve on the Committee on Manufacturing Innovation of the National Academy of Engineering; and on the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research (CIFAR). She served on the Nanotechnology & Scientific Advisory Boards of Lockheed Martin and PepsiCo Corporations.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.internano.org/nms/2013/goel | title=Dr. Anita Goel, MD, Ph.D. &#124; Nanomanufacturing Summit|website=Internano.org }}</ref>

As the chairman and CEO of Nanobiosym Diagnostics (NBSDx), Goel oversees product design, engineering, clinical trials, regulatory approvals and manufacturing of the company's breakthrough technologies, such as the Gene-RADAR and its “apps” for personalized precision medicine, digital health and global health security. In 2020, Barclay's Bank<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.theatlantic.com/sponsored/barclays-unreasonable-group-2020/entrepreneurship-force-good/3553/ | title=Entrepreneurship as a Force for Good | website=[[The Atlantic]] }}</ref> and the Unreasonable Group selected Nanobiosym Dx amongst the “World’s Top 10 Companies solving the Global COVID Crisis” and Scientific American<ref>{{cite web | url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/precision-mobile-testing-is-key-to-opening-the-economy-safely/ | title=Precision Mobile Testing is Key to Opening the Economy Safely|website=Blogs.scientificamerican.com}}</ref> featured her work on how mobile precision testing for COVID could safely re-open the US and global economy.

== Awards ==
Named as one of the World's "Top 35 science and technology innovators" by MIT Technology Review<ref>{{cite web |title=Anita Goel |url=https://lemelson.mit.edu/resources/anita-goel |website=Lemelson.mit.edu}}</ref> and one of the "World's Most Influential Visionaries in Biotech" by Scientific American<ref>{{cite web |title=Who Are The Most Influential People in Biotech Today |url=https://static.scientificamerican.com/wv/assets/2015_SAWorldView.pdf |access-date=21 July 2022 |website=Static.scientificamerican.com}}</ref> Goel has been recognized with three DARPA Breakthrough Awards, two USAID Grand Challenge Awards,<ref>{{cite web |title=Nanobiosym Pilot: Optimization and Evaluation of Gene-RADAR® Nanotech platform Point-Of-Care HIV Diagnostic Device Prevention of Mother-To-Child Transmission in Rwanda |url=https://savinglivesatbirth.net/nanobiosym-pilot-optimization-and-evaluation-of-gene-radar-nanotech-platform-point-of-care-hiv-diagnostic-device-prevention-of-mother-to-child-transmission-in-rwanda/ |access-date=21 July 2022 |website=Savinglifesatbirth.net}}</ref> NASA's Galactic Challenge Award,<ref>{{cite web |title=SpaceX Will Launch MRSA Samples to International Space Station |url=https://www.inverse.com/article/27576-spacex-superbug-mrsa-space-station-iss |website=Inverse.com|date=8 February 2017 }}</ref> and multiple awards from DOD, DOE, AFOSR, and NSF.
